explains: format_cents changes in the shared library libs/common/acme_common/money.py (cents_to_decimal in the same file is untouched). Importers of acme_common.money, each resolved from its own service root (billing and cases both have a package called app, so module names are resolved per service marker): (1) services/billing/app/services/settlement.py imports it through a multi-line parenthesised import (from acme_common.money import ( cents_to_decimal, format_cents, )) and calls format_cents(total_cents); (2) services/billing/app/routers/invoices.py imports the name under an alias (format_cents as fmt_cents) and calls fmt_cents(invoice.amount_cents); (3) services/cases/app/routers/cases.py imports the module under an alias (import acme_common.money as money_utils) and calls money_utils.format_cents(row.exposure_cents). services/billing/app/jobs.py imports only cents_to_decimal from the same module, so it is not a caller of format_cents. services/billing/tests/test_money.py imports format_cents but a unit test is a test, not a caller: it is listed as a unit test. services/billing/tests/test_settlement.py imports the settlement service, not the library, so it is not a caller either. Callers are the direct importers and call sites of the changed function; the routes and screens those callers reach are transitive reach, not callers, and are not claimed here.
